newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TNT confident of higher 96/97 profits.
newsitem.headline: TNT confident of higher 96/97 profits.

text.p: Transport group TNT Ltd said on Wednesday it remained confident of improved profits in 1996/97.

"Following the disposal of our Spanish and Brazilian road operations, closure of the Australian LCL business and with completion of the Ansett sale imminent, the company is in a better position to capitalise on the success of global logistics and time-sensitive businesses," TNT said in releasing its annual results.
"We remain confident of improved profits in 1996/97," TNT said.
TNT earlier announced that its equity accounted net profit tumbled to A$9.84 million in 1995/96 (July-June) from A$40.01 million in 1994/95.

Earlier TNT reported a 23 percent fall in operating profit before tax for the year to June 30 to A$93.2 million. Net profit fell to A$9.84 million from A$40.01 million and net profit before abnormals but after preference dividends fell to A$0.6 million from A$38.48 million in 1994/95.
Analysts had expected a pre-abnormal, post preferences loss of between A$4 million and A$22 million.
TNT said the profit drop principally reflected a lower contribution from the Ansett group, partially offset by an improved result from GD Express Worldwide.
"TNT's core businesses of domestic time-sensitive freight and logistics recorded 21.8 percent growth in revenues and 33.5 percent (growth) in profits for the year," TNT said.
"However, the improved contribution from these activities was offset by disappointing performances from non-time sensitive freight operations in Australia and Brazil," it said.
"The lower pre-tax contribution on an equity consolidated basis stemmed from a significantly lower contribution from Ansett, partially offset by improved profitability of GD Express Worldwide."
TNT this week finalised the sale of its 50 percent stake in Ansett Australia to Air New Zealand in a deal that would generate cash receipts of A$325 million for TNT.
TNT's net profit included an abnormal loss of A$65.38 million, compared with a A$9.47 million loss the previous year.

TNT said the abnormal loss related mainly to provisions made for the cost of certain Australian non-time sensitive businesses and the sale of the Spanish freigh operations and certain shipping interests.
"Equity consolidated abnormal items include unrealised currency translation gains and asset write downs in the Ansett group."
TNT said Ansett reported a significantly lower contribution, but jet leasing firm Ansett Worldwide, which TNT owns jointly with News Corp Ltd, had an improved profit for the year.
TNT's shares were up one cent at A$1.45 at 10.50 a.m. (0050 GMT).
